Jest runs the callback of `describe` right away to collect the tests inside it. It does not wait for a promise, so a test declared after an `await` is not collected. It passes no arguments to the callback, and the callback must not return a value.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}
```ts
import { describe, expect, test } from "@jest/globals";

describe("cart", async () => {
  const items = await loadItems();

  test("has items", () => {
    expect(items.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });
});
```

{/* bad {"count": 5} */}
```ts
import { describe, test } from "@jest/globals";

describe("cart"); // no callback

describe("cart", "adds an item"); // not a function

describe("cart", (done) => {
  test("adds an item", () => {});
  done(); // the callback gets no arguments
});

describe("cart", () => {
  return test("adds an item", () => {});
});

describe("cart", () => test("adds an item", () => {})); // returns the result of `test()`
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```ts
import { beforeAll, describe, expect, test } from "@jest/globals";

describe("cart", () => {
  let items;

  beforeAll(async () => {
    items = await loadItems();
  });

  test("has items", () => {
    expect(items.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });
});
```

The callback of `describe.each` gets the values of a row, so it can have parameters:

{/* good */}
```ts
import { describe, expect, test } from "@jest/globals";

describe.each([1, 2, 3])("cart with %i items", (count) => {
  test("counts them", () => {
    expect(fill(count).length).toBe(count);
  });
});
```

## When not to use it

The rule only looks at the call, so a callback passed by name is reported as not being a function. Turn the rule off if you share groups of tests that way:

{/* bad */}
```ts
import { describe } from "@jest/globals";
import { cartTests } from "./shared";

describe("cart", cartTests);
```
